chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Saif ibn Umayra from Mansur who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Regarding the woman whose husband dies or divorces her while he is absent, he said: If he is at a distance of a few days' journey, she begins her waiting period from the day her husband dies. If he is far away, she begins from the day the news reaches her, because she must mourn for him.

key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: Waiting period (iddah) for a woman after divorce or death of husband
key_terms.مَسِيرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: Distance of a few days' journey

ai.seo_question: When does a woman's waiting period begin if her husband dies while he is away?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the commencement of the waiting period (iddah) for a woman whose husband dies or divorces her while absent depends on proximity: it begins from the day of death if he is nearby, but from the day news reaches her if he is distant. This ruling ensures the practical observance of mourning (hudd) despite the logistical delay in communication, reflecting the juristic principle of ease in applying religious obligations.
